title: O jabuti e a onça
author: Sílvio Romero (collector)
sourceEdition: Contos Populares do Brasil (1885), public-domain Brazilian folk tale
sourceJurisdiction: Public domain worldwide (collector died 1914; traditional tale)

premise.en: A clever little tortoise makes a flute from an old bone and outsmarts a hungry jaguar in the Brazilian forest.
premise.fr: Une petite tortue rusée fabrique une flûte avec un vieil os et déjoue un jaguar affamé dans la forêt brésilienne.
premise.es: Una pequeña y astuta tortuga fabrica una flauta con un hueso viejo y engaña a un jaguar hambriento en la selva brasileña.

summary.en: The slow tortoise finds an old hollow bone and crafts a musical flute that charms the animals of the forest. When a ferocious jaguar comes to hunt him, the tortoise uses quick thinking and a hollow tree to protect himself. Through wit rather than strength, the small creature triumphs over the dangerous predator.
summary.fr: La lente tortue trouve un vieil os creux et fabrique une flûte musicale qui enchante les animaux de la forêt. Quand un féroce jaguar s'approche pour la chasser, la tortue utilise son intelligence et un arbre creux pour se protéger. Grâce à la ruse plutôt qu'à la force, la petite créature triomphe du dangereux prédateur.
summary.es: La lenta tortuga encuentra un viejo hueso hueco y fabrica una flauta musical que encanta a los animales del bosque. Cuando un feroz jaguar se acerca para cazarla, la tortuga usa su ingenio y un árbol hueco para protegerse. Mediante la astucia en lugar de la fuerza, la pequeña criatura triunfa sobre el peligroso depredador.

tutorNotes.pronunciation: Pay special attention to nasal vowels such as 'onça' (/ˈõ.sɐ/), 'não' (/nɐ̃w̃/), and 'chão' (/ʃɐ̃w̃/), where air must flow through the nose. Notice the open 'é' (/ɛ/) in 'é' versus the closed or reduced 'e'. The digraph 'lh' in 'velha' sounds like /ʎ/ (similar to 'million'), and final 'r' in verbs like 'agir' and 'comer' is typically an aspirated /h/ or silent in colloquial Brazilian Portuguese.
tutorNotes.grammar: This text demonstrates basic Brazilian Portuguese present tense regular verbs ('vive', 'caminha', 'sopra', 'começa') along with high-frequency irregular verbs like 'é' (ser) and 'tem' (ter). Observe standard prepositional contractions: 'de' + 'o' becomes 'do', 'de' + 'a' becomes 'da', and 'em' + 'o' becomes 'no'. Pronoun and clitic usage reflects natural Brazilian Portuguese word order.
tutorNotes.culture: The jabuti (land tortoise) is the quintessential trickster hero of indigenous and Brazilian folk traditions, famously documented in Sílvio Romero's 1885 collection. In contrast to European fables where turtles represent slow persistence, Brazilian folklore celebrates the jabuti for his intellectual cunning against top predators like the jaguar (onça-pintada). The motif of crafting a musical flute from found bones is a traditional folk element emphasizing resourcefulness.
tutorNotes.commonErrors: Learners frequently confuse the verbs 'ser' and 'estar'; here, 'é' describes permanent characteristics ('o jabuti é sábio') while 'está' marks temporary states or locations ('está longe do perigo'). Another frequent error is pronouncing the letter 'o' at the end of words as a full English 'oh', whereas in Brazilian Portuguese unstressed final 'o' reduces to a short /u/ sound (e.g., 'bicho', 'osso', 'buraco').
